questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise, because Sydney and Melbourne couldn't agree on which of them should be the capital.

questions.question: Which river flows through the Amazon rainforest?
questions.fact: The Amazon carries more water than any other river: roughly a fifth of all river water flowing into the world's oceans.

questions.question: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.fact: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as Canada's capital in 1857, partly because it sat between English- and French-speaking areas.

questions.question: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.fact: Italy's "boot" even has a heel (Puglia) and a toe (Calabria), which looks like it is kicking Sicily.

questions.question: In which country is Machu Picchu?
questions.fact: The Inca built Machu Picchu in the 1400s. It was little known to the outside world until 1911.

questions.question: What is the largest country in the world by area?
questions.fact: Russia spans 11 time zones, and its area is slightly bigger than the whole surface of Pluto.

questions.question: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.fact: The Sahara is about the size of the United States. Thousands of years ago it was green, with lakes and grasslands.

questions.question: Mount Everest sits on the border of Nepal and which country?
questions.fact: Everest is called Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet.

questions.question: Which Spanish city is home to the Sagrada Família?
questions.fact: The Sagrada Família has been under construction since 1882. Gaudí worked on it for over 40 years, until his death in 1926.

questions.question: What is the capital of Portugal?
questions.fact: Much of Lisbon was destroyed by a huge earthquake and tsunami in 1755, and the centre was rebuilt on a neat grid.

questions.question: According to UN estimates, which country became the most populous in 2023?
questions.fact: India and China each have more than 1.4 billion people, together more than a third of everyone on Earth.

questions.question: Which city is nicknamed "the Big Apple"?
questions.fact: "The Big Apple" was made popular in the 1920s by a sports writer who used it for New York's horse races.

questions.question: Which river flows through Paris?
questions.fact: Paris has 37 bridges across the Seine. The oldest standing one is ironically called the Pont Neuf, "the New Bridge".

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which country?
questions.fact: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest structure built by living things on Earth, and it is visible from space.

questions.question: In which country is the city of Marrakech?
questions.fact: Marrakech is nicknamed "the Red City" because of its red sandstone walls and buildings.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world?
questions.fact: Vatican City covers only about 0.44 km², smaller than many city parks, yet it has its own post office and radio station.

questions.question: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
questions.fact: The Indian Ocean is the warmest of the world's oceans.

questions.question: Which European country is famous for its fjords?
questions.fact: Norway's longest fjord, the Sognefjord, reaches over 200 km inland.

questions.question: Which is the largest of the Canary Islands?
questions.fact: Tenerife is home to Mount Teide and some of Europe's clearest skies, which is why it has a major astronomy observatory.

questions.question: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.fact: Greater Tokyo, with about 37 million people, is often called the biggest metropolitan area in the world.

questions.question: The Andes mountains run along which continent?
questions.fact: The Andes are the longest mountain range on any continent, stretching about 7,000 km.

questions.question: What currency is used in Japan?
questions.fact: Japan's 1-yen coin is made of aluminium and is so light it can float on water.

questions.question: Which small country sits in the Pyrenees between Spain and France?
questions.fact: Andorra has two heads of state at the same time: a Spanish bishop and the President of France.

questions.question: Which US state is made up entirely of islands?
questions.fact: Hawaii is the only US state entirely in the tropics. Its Mauna Kea is taller than Everest if you measure from the sea floor.

questions.question: What is the capital of Egypt?
questions.fact: Cairo is nicknamed "the city of a thousand minarets", and the Pyramids of Giza stand on its edge.

questions.question: Which city lies on both sides of the Bosphorus, in Europe and Asia?
questions.fact: Istanbul was called Byzantium and then Constantinople before it got its current name.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain in Spain?
questions.fact: Teide is 3,715 metres tall. Measured from the ocean floor it is one of the tallest volcanoes on Earth.

questions.question: Lake Titicaca lies on the border of Peru and which country?
questions.fact: At about 3,800 metres up, Lake Titicaca is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.

questions.question: Which Spanish city is famous for the Alhambra palace?
questions.fact: "Alhambra" comes from Arabic for "the red one", after the reddish colour of its walls.

questions.question: What is the capital of Iceland?
questions.fact: Reykjavik is the northernmost capital of a sovereign country in the world.

questions.question: What is the capital of Germany?
questions.fact: Berlin is said to have more bridges than Venice, around 900 of them.

questions.question: What is the capital of Turkey?
questions.fact: Ankara replaced Istanbul as Turkey's capital in 1923, when Atatürk founded the republic.

questions.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.fact: Brasília was built from scratch in about four years and became the capital in 1960. From above, its layout looks like a plane.

questions.question: What is the capital of Argentina?
questions.fact: Buenos Aires means "good airs" or "fair winds". Its Avenida 9 de Julio is one of the widest avenues in the world.

questions.question: What is the capital of Morocco?
questions.fact: Many people guess Casablanca, Morocco's biggest city. But the capital is Rabat.

questions.question: What is the capital of Switzerland?
questions.fact: Switzerland's constitution names no capital at all; Bern is officially just the "federal city".

questions.question: What is the capital of New Zealand?
questions.fact: Wellington is the southernmost capital of a sovereign country, and it's famously windy.

questions.question: What is the capital of South Korea?
questions.fact: Seoul has been Korea's capital for over 600 years, since 1394.

questions.question: What is the capital of Ireland?
questions.fact: Dublin's name comes from the Irish "Dubh Linn", meaning "black pool".

questions.question: What is the capital of Poland?
questions.fact: Warsaw's old town was almost destroyed in World War II and rebuilt so faithfully that it is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: What is the capital of Greece?
questions.fact: Legend says Athena won the city by giving it an olive tree, beating Poseidon's gift, and the city was named after her.

questions.question: What is the capital of Mexico?
questions.fact: Mexico City is built on an old lake bed, and some parts of it sink several centimetres every year.

questions.question: What is the capital of Peru?
questions.fact: Francisco Pizarro founded Lima in 1535 and called it the "City of Kings".

questions.question: What is the capital of Colombia?
questions.fact: Bogotá sits about 2,640 metres above sea level, one of the highest capitals in the world.

questions.question: What is the capital of Austria?
questions.fact: Vienna's coffee house culture is so special that UNESCO lists it as cultural heritage.

questions.question: What is the capital of Norway?
questions.fact: Every December, the Nobel Peace Prize is presented in Oslo City Hall.

questions.question: What is the capital of Finland?
questions.fact: Helsinki has around 300 islands just off its coast.

questions.question: What is the capital of Thailand?
questions.fact: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world, over 160 letters when written in English.

questions.question: What is the capital of Scotland?
questions.fact: Edinburgh Castle sits on Castle Rock, the plug of an extinct volcano.

questions.question: What is the capital of Wales?
questions.fact: Cardiff only became the capital of Wales in 1955, making it one of Europe's youngest capitals.

questions.question: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
questions.fact: Canada's coastline is about 240,000 km long, enough to circle the Equator about six times.

questions.question: What is the largest island in the world that isn't a continent?
questions.fact: About 80% of Greenland is covered by ice. Despite the names, it is much icier than Iceland.

questions.question: Greenland is an autonomous territory of which country?
questions.fact: Greenland has only about 56,000 people, which makes it the most sparsely populated territory in the world.

questions.question: What is the longest river in Europe?
questions.fact: The Volga flows about 3,500 km through Russia before emptying into the Caspian Sea.

questions.question: Which river flows through Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade?
questions.fact: The Danube flows through ten countries, more than any other river in the world.

questions.question: What is the largest country in Africa by area?
questions.fact: Algeria became Africa's largest country when Sudan split in two in 2011. More than 80% of it is Sahara desert.

questions.question: What is the most populous country in Africa?
questions.fact: Nigeria has over 220 million people, and its film industry, "Nollywood", makes more films each year than Hollywood.

questions.question: Counting its overseas territories, which country has the most time zones?
questions.fact: Thanks to overseas territories like French Polynesia and Réunion, France covers 12 time zones.

questions.question: Which continent has the most countries?
questions.fact: Africa has 54 countries recognised by the UN.

questions.question: Which two countries share the longest border in the world?
questions.fact: The Canada–USA border is about 8,900 km long, and a big part of it follows a straight line along the 49th parallel.

questions.question: Which sea has no coastline at all?
questions.fact: The Sargasso Sea is in the Atlantic, bordered only by ocean currents, and named after the floating sargassum seaweed.

questions.question: What is the largest lake in the world by area?
questions.fact: The Caspian Sea is called a sea but is really a lake, shared by five countries.

questions.question: What is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.fact: Lake Baikal in Siberia is over 1,600 metres deep and holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.

questions.question: Which long, thin country runs down South America's west coast?
questions.fact: Chile is about 4,300 km long but on average only about 180 km wide.

questions.question: Which European country is nicknamed "the Hexagon" because of its shape?
questions.fact: Mainland France has six rough sides, three along the sea and three along land borders.

questions.question: What is the line at 0° longitude called?
questions.fact: Greenwich was chosen as the Prime Meridian at an international conference in Washington in 1884.

questions.question: The Prime Meridian passes through which part of London?
questions.fact: At the Royal Observatory in Greenwich you can stand with one foot in the eastern hemisphere and one in the western.

questions.question: Which South American country is named after the Equator?
questions.fact: Ecuador's famous equator monument, "Mitad del Mundo", turned out to be about 240 metres away from the real line, according to GPS.

questions.question: Which country is famous for tulips and windmills?
questions.fact: The Netherlands is famous for tulips, but they first came from Central Asia, by way of the Ottoman Empire.

questions.question: Patagonia is shared by Chile and which other country?
questions.fact: Patagonia covers about a million square kilometres of glaciers, steppe and mountains like the Torres del Paine.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain range in the world?
questions.fact: The Himalayas hold most of the world's highest peaks, including Everest. Their name means "home of snow" in Sanskrit.

questions.question: Mont Blanc is the highest peak of which mountain range?
questions.fact: Mont Blanc is about 4,800 metres high and sits on the border between France and Italy.

questions.question: Which country has the most active volcanoes?
questions.fact: Indonesia has more than 120 active volcanoes because it sits on the Pacific "Ring of Fire".

questions.question: Mount Etna is on which island?
questions.fact: Etna is one of the most active volcanoes on Earth and the tallest active volcano in Europe, about 3,300 metres high.

questions.question: Which is the largest US state by area?
questions.fact: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas. The USA bought it from Russia in 1867 for $7.2 million.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in South America?
questions.fact: Suriname is the only country in South America where Dutch is the official language.

questions.question: Madagascar is an island off the coast of which continent?
questions.fact: About 90% of Madagascar's wildlife lives nowhere else on Earth, including all of its lemurs.

questions.question: The Bermuda Triangle is in which ocean?
questions.fact: Studies have found that ships don't vanish in the Bermuda Triangle any more often than in other busy stretches of sea.

questions.question: Which canal connects the Mediterranean and the Red Sea?
questions.fact: The Suez Canal opened in 1869 and saves ships sailing between Europe and Asia the long trip around Africa.

questions.question: The Panama Canal connects which two oceans?
questions.fact: Locks lift ships in the Panama Canal about 26 metres up to Gatun Lake and lower them down again on the other side.

questions.question: Which country has more ancient pyramids than Egypt?
questions.fact: Sudan has over 200 ancient pyramids, built by the Kingdom of Kush. They are smaller and steeper than Egypt's.

questions.question: Which is the driest non-polar desert in the world?
questions.fact: Some weather stations in the Atacama have never recorded rain, and NASA tests Mars rovers there because it looks so like Mars.

questions.question: Which is the largest Scandinavian country by area?
questions.fact: Sweden has nearly 100,000 lakes.

questions.question: Which country borders Spain to the west?
questions.fact: The border between Spain and Portugal, "La Raya", is one of Europe's oldest, largely unchanged since a treaty in 1297.

questions.question: Which EU country has the most people?
questions.fact: Germany has about 84 million people, the most of any EU country.

questions.question: What is the largest country in the EU by area?
questions.fact: Mainland France covers about 550,000 km², and overseas regions like French Guiana make it even bigger.

questions.question: By area, Spain is the EU's…
questions.fact: Spain covers about 506,000 km², and it is one of the most mountainous countries in Europe.

questions.question: What is the capital of Denmark?
questions.fact: Copenhagen's Tivoli Gardens, opened in 1843, is one of the oldest amusement parks in the world.

questions.question: What is the capital of the Netherlands?
questions.fact: Amsterdam is the official capital, but the Dutch government and parliament sit in The Hague.

questions.question: What is the capital of Croatia?
questions.fact: Zagreb has a Museum of Broken Relationships, full of objects people donated after break-ups.

questions.question: What is the capital of Vietnam?
questions.fact: Hanoi means "inside the rivers". The city is over 1,000 years old.
